acceptance: With the product's inputs CSV parses quoted delimiters, escaped quotes and multiline cells; a serialized snapshot reparses to the same cells; `.tsv` and tab-heavy samples choose the tab delimiter; malformed quoted source keeps its cells and reports the unclosed quote; newline and BOM conventions survive an edit; a terminal empty one-column record survives; rows normalize to a rectangle, header inference follows the product's rules and columns are labelled A…Z, AA (the product's trimRows has no caller).

A cell edit replaces only its row and serializes on demand (the same text object until the next change); accepted source stays byte-exact until a local edit and a replacement is taken as written; row and column identities follow their moves; undo and redo belong to the model; one edit in a 500 × 20 table shares every other row.

The header stays fixed while rows move by command or drop; body rows insert, duplicate and delete without touching the source; columns move, insert and delete whole; deleting the only row leaves a blank one; expanding grows rows and columns at once and never shrinks; capacity caps refuse overflow.

Column widths are view state: they catch up with the document whenever the view syncs (also after columns were added while it was away, and on undo), never follow cell content, follow column identities through a move, a delete and its undo, restore compatible stored widths without entering the CSV, cap only initial and reset widths (an explicit width is kept) and fit proportionally while keeping readable minimums; widths for CSV and Markdown share one visual-width model sampled from at most 128 rows including the last.

Corner drags snap outward distance to whole rows and columns once past a track's midpoint, never shrink and stop at the remaining budget; added rows are capped by the canvas below the table while columns may grow past its edge; edge scrolling runs only at the outward edge at a bounded speed (left to right; the mirrored right-to-left case belongs to rtl-writing-direction).

Header interpretation, row numbers and column widths are kept per document without disturbing each other or a sibling document; a malformed store or a missing document id reads as empty and writes nothing; widths come back only for the same delimiter and column count.

reason: TS mounts a bounded window of DOM rows and columns (prefix geometry for variable widths, a mounted-item cap, directional and velocity-predicted overscan) so fast scrolling stays inside rendered rows. The native grid paints exactly the rows and columns that intersect the viewport on every frame, so there are no mounted items, caps or overscan to predict; large-table cost is covered by the CSV view tests (large_csv_parses_in_background_while_showing_readonly_preview_and_respects_replace_text) and the csv_table_cost bench.
